_meta.purpose: Surfaces the non-property-tax revenue sources already present in county-budget-fy2025-26.json (Non-Departmental section) but not yet explained in the app. Most residents assume county government runs entirely on property tax -- it doesn't.
_meta.source: Same FY2025-26 proposed budget PDF already used for county-budget-fy2025-26.json, Non-Departmental revenue lines.

headline: Property tax is Curry County government's single biggest revenue source, but it's well under half the story -- federal timber payments, tourism tax, and several smaller fees and shared state taxes round out the rest.

revenue_sources.name: Property tax (County General)
revenue_sources.plain_explanation: The county's own permanent tax rate, already covered elsewhere in this app -- about 7 cents of every property tax dollar residents pay countywide.

revenue_sources.name: O&C Timber Payments
revenue_sources.plain_explanation: A federal payment tied to "O&C lands" -- former Oregon & California Railroad land grant timberland that the federal government now manages and shares timber-harvest-related revenue from with the counties it sits in. This is a distinctly Oregon-coast-counties story, not something most U.S. counties receive.
revenue_sources.note_worth_flagging: The county's FY2025-26 budget message states Curry County received NO Secure Rural Schools (SRS) funds this year and instead elected to take O&C timber payments -- SRS is a related but separate federal safety-net program for timber counties, and its funding has been uncertain/lapsing in recent years. This is a genuine budget risk worth explaining: a meaningful chunk of county revenue depends on federal decisions Curry County doesn't control.

revenue_sources.name: Federal Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILT)
revenue_sources.plain_explanation: A federal payment that compensates counties for having large amounts of tax-exempt federal land within their borders (national forests, BLM land, etc.) -- land the county can't collect property tax on, so the federal government sends a substitute payment instead.

revenue_sources.name: Transient Lodging Tax (TLT)
revenue_sources.plain_explanation: A tax on hotel, campground, and short-term rental stays -- paid mostly by visitors, not residents. In early 2025 the Board of Commissioners raised the TLT rate; the increase is estimated to add about $700,000 to the General Fund and about $1.6 million specifically earmarked for tourism and economic development uses (by law, a portion of lodging tax revenue has to go toward tourism promotion, not general spending).
revenue_sources.note_worth_flagging: This is a good 'visitors help pay for county services too' fact for a tourism-dependent coastal county.

revenue_sources.name: Electric Co-Op Franchise Fees
revenue_sources.plain_explanation: A fee the county charges the local electric cooperative for use of public rights-of-way.

revenue_sources.name: State-Shared Marijuana Tax
revenue_sources.plain_explanation: Curry County's share of Oregon's statewide marijuana tax, distributed back to counties and cities.

revenue_sources.name: State-Shared Alcohol Tax
revenue_sources.plain_explanation: Curry County's share of Oregon's statewide alcohol tax revenue.

revenue_sources.name: Cable Franchise Fees
revenue_sources.plain_explanation: A fee charged to cable providers for use of public infrastructure.

revenue_sources.name: State-Shared Tobacco Tax
revenue_sources.plain_explanation: Curry County's share of Oregon's statewide tobacco tax.

app_display_guidance.suggested_placement: A distinct section or toggle near the 'County Government' category -- e.g. 'Where county government's OTHER money comes from' -- since this is genuinely surprising to most residents and a strong complement to the existing 'only 7 cents of your tax dollar' framing.
app_display_guidance.suggested_visual: A simple bar or donut chart of these revenue sources, separate from the property-tax-by-district chart already in the app, since mixing the two would conflate 'what residents pay in property tax' with 'everything the county collects from all sources.'
app_display_guidance.good_pull_quote: Curry County received zero federal Secure Rural Schools (SRS) funding this year -- a reminder that timber-dependent Oregon coastal counties still depend heavily on federal decisions made far from Gold Beach.
